instantiated_cells.justification: §101.72(A) requires each legislative agent and employer to file an initial registration statement within ten days following an engagement, and §101.71(A) makes it unlawful for a legislative agent or employer to knowingly fail to register as required.

§101.72(F) provides that the registration card and the legislative agent's registration shall be valid from the date of issuance until the next thirty-first day of December of an even-numbered year, meaning registration must be renewed biennially (approximately every 24 months).

§101.72(D)(1) requires changes in required information to be reflected in the next updated registration statement (filed in Jan/May/Sept), and (D)(2) requires written notification of termination within thirty days; the explicit numeric change-notification deadline in the statute is 30 days for termination.
§101.72(A) requires each legislative agent and employer, within ten days following an engagement of a legislative agent, to file an initial registration statement.
§101.72(A) requires "each legislative agent and employer" to file an initial registration statement, imposing separate filing obligations on both the lobbyist and the employer/principal.

§101.72(A) enumerates the required contents of the initial registration statement (name, business address, occupation, employer info, description of legislation) and does not require submission of a photograph.

§101.72(E) provides that an officer or employee of a state agency who actively advocates in a fiduciary capacity as a representative of that state agency need not file expenditure statements under §101.73, creating a partial exemption for government officials acting in their official capacity.

§101.72(E) relieves state-agency officers/employees who actively advocate in a fiduciary capacity from filing expenditure statements under §101.73, a partial exemption from the regulatory regime applied to private lobbyists.
